named_beneficiary.support: חילופים בין ראש הממשלה וראש הממשלה החלופי ייערכו... יום לאחר שהתקבל בכנסת בקריאה השלישית חוק על התפזרות הכנסת
named_beneficiary.note: Beneficiary: the sitting alternation government and its alternate Prime Minister (Yair Lapid, per press), whose swap is secured on dissolution or budget failure, plus two deputy ministers in the PM's office. Text is drafted generally for 'ממשלת חילופים'; the sitting government was the only one. Government bill ה"ח הממשלה 1410 of 28.6.2021; explanatory notes unreachable.

immediate_effect.support: Sections 1-4 only; no commencement clause; passed 27.7.2021, published 28.7.2021
immediate_effect.note: basis: by absence of a clause

coalition_only.source: Walla, 27.7.2021, https://www.walla.co.il/news/politics/3450734; Times of Israel 27.7.2021; en.wikipedia Thirty-sixth government of Israel
coalition_only.support: '61 תומכים מול 2 מתנגדים'; 'גיוס מלא של 61 ח"כים'; 'רוב חברי האופוזיציה נעדרו מההצבעה לאחר שנטשו במהלך הדיון'
coalition_only.note: Outside the tables' coverage; no faction breakdown published. The 61 for equal the coalition's full mobilization (Yesh Atid, Blue and White, Yamina, Labor, Yisrael Beiteinu, New Hope, Meretz, Ra'am; 62 seats formally); search summaries attribute the two against to the Joint List; no opposition member reported voting for. Coded Yes on that basis.

expedited.note: The Knesset Committee also set 'סדרי דיון מיוחדים... לפי סעיף 98 לתקנון הכנסת' for the second and third reading (plenary debate, not the committee stage).

scope.support: Adds swap triggers (s. 43A1) and two deputy ministers in the PM's office (ss. 25(a), 43E(a))
scope.note: The Knesset's power to dissolve itself and the budget deadline are untouched; no check or right removed.

targets_judiciary.support: Subject: alternation government and deputy ministers

deviation_tier.support: Swap occurs if dissolution passes with votes of at least two MKs from factions affiliated with the PM
deviation_tier.note: Principal engagement: separation of powers (executive succession rules). Coded as not contradicting; 'Limited' is arguable because the trigger is tailored to the sitting coalition's pact.

Coalition on 14.12.2023: Likud, Shas, UTJ, Religious Zionism, Otzma Yehudit, Noam, plus National Unity (joined the emergency government 11.10.2023); opposition: Yesh Atid, Yisrael Beiteinu, Ra'am, Hadash-Ta'al, Labor.

scope.support: Postponement limited to one period of up to 50 days, with Knesset approval on the Finance Committee's recommendation
scope.note: The convergence mechanism and its automatic cuts remain; Knesset approval is the alternative mechanism.

deviation_tier.support: Deadline postponement subject to Knesset approval after an unforeseen fiscal event
deviation_tier.note: Engages separation of powers (fiscal discipline check) without contradicting it, since the Knesset must approve.

final_vote_record.source: Knesset legal adviser letter 11.1.2024 ('שאושר בקריאה השניה ובקריאה השלישית... ביום 14/12/2023'); Kipa and JDN 14.12.2023
final_vote_record.note: Outside the tables' coverage. Kipa/JDN describe three bills approved together (this amendment, Deficit Reduction Law Amendment 24, supplementary 2023 budget) and give one tally; whether one vote approved all three is not stated. MK Edelstein asked to change his vote to abstain.

deviations: Knesset servers (fs.knesset.gov.il, knesset.gov.il) redirect to a geo maintenance page, and WebFetch cannot reach web.archive.org; the sheet's archived gazette PDFs were therefore pulled with curl from the same archive captures (raw 'if_' form) and their text extracted with macOS PDFKit, without saving files. Extraction garbles some digits and a few words (noted where relevant).

No explanatory notes were reachable for any enactment (bill PDFs not captured by the archive; Knesset site down), so named_beneficiary is coded from the enactment text, with press reports of the vote used only to identify who the text refers to (seq 97, 112).

Verbatim gazette text could not be retrieved for seq 105 (no capture of 23_lsr_576894.pdf) and seq 118 (no archived document); those rows rely on Nevo's and Wikisource's consolidated texts as summarised by the fetch tool, a Knesset legal adviser's letter mirrored at next.obudget.org (used for the 14.12.2023 reading date and the provision's wording), and press.
Government composition taken from English and Hebrew Wikipedia articles on the 31st, 33rd, 34th, 35th, 36th and 37th governments, as the sheet allows when the Knesset site is unreachable.

Dates of first readings taken from the Knesset's plenum-session tables (kns_plmsessionitem, kns_plenumsession, kns_status) and bills table (kns_bill) as mirrored at production.oknesset.org/pipelines/data/, treated as Knesset records; committee-session tables used the same way for seq 118. Vote tables for 2015-07-30 and 2018-01-10 were read from the Open Knesset mirror (view_vote_rslts_hdr_approved, including member-ID lists) and member names from its members tables.
Nevo gazette-issue PDFs returned a block page; Nevo consolidated pages were read only through the fetch tool's summariser, which did not expose the amendment-history block.

Pages closed: none opened were about a court case. Some search-result summaries mentioned litigation (a High Court warning concerning the 2020 budget amendments; a 2015 ruling about a deputy minister; a petition on the 2021 rotation law); those pages were not opened and nothing from the summaries was used. The Maariv article fetched for seq 89 concerned the 2020 'Norwegian law' and was discarded.
Not found: the final-reading tally for seq 76; the first-reading date for seq 118; faction breakdowns of the final votes for seq 97, 112 and 118 (press tallies only).

seq 89: the vote tables have no final-approval row for the Basic Law itself; coalition_only rests on the companion law's final vote (22410) and the Basic Law's last committee-proposal vote (22392), which list the same 64 members voting for.

Identification of individual members in seq 97's note (Rosenthal, Levy-Abekasis) comes from matching vote-table member IDs to the mirrored members table; their factions are taken from the sheet's breakdown and the ynetnews report, not from a faction table.
